name: google-calendar-list-events
description:
List upcoming events from a Google Calendar over a time window. Returns structured event data (summary, start, end, location, attendees, hangout_link) and, for each event, what a planner needs: whether it holds the time (`busy`), its kind (`event_type`: default, focusTime, outOfOffice, workingLocation …), the calendar owner's own answer (`response`), how many other people are invited (`guests`), and the invitation's `uid`, which is the same on every calendar the invitation sits on. `truncated` is true when the calendar holds more events in the window than were returned. Canonical building block for morning-brief / meeting-prep / schedule-awareness workflows.

Requires a vault:// reference to a Google OAuth access token in the AUTH_HEADER config key. The controller resolves + refreshes the token at dispatch time.

AUTH_HEADER.description: vault:// path to the OAuth access token wrapped in 'Bearer ' (e.g. 'Bearer vault://oauth/google_calendar/{user_id}/{account_id}/access_token'). The controller resolves + refreshes the token if expired.

CALENDAR_ID.description: Calendar ID. 'primary' for the authenticated user's main calendar, or a specific calendar address / ID.

HOURS_AHEAD.description: Window size in hours (1–336, i.e. up to 14 days). Events starting between now and now+HOURS_AHEAD are returned.

MAX_RESULTS.description: Maximum events to return (1–250; default 20). Costs roughly 140–270K fuel per event (more for events with long descriptions): above 50, set `max_fuel` on the node. When the calendar holds more, the output's `truncated` is true.

TIME_ZONE.description: Optional IANA zone name (e.g. 'America/New_York'). Start and end times are then returned in that zone's local time with its UTC offset, so a module can group events by local day without a time-zone database, across daylight-saving changes. Omitted: the calendar's own zone. The zone used is echoed as `time_zone`.

setup_instructions.title: Enable the Google Calendar API
setup_instructions.detail: In https://console.cloud.google.com, enable the Google Calendar API and configure OAuth consent with the 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly' scope.

setup_instructions.title: Authorize the integration
setup_instructions.detail: Complete the OAuth flow via your Talos integration UI or CLI. The controller stores tokens at 'oauth/google_calendar/{user_id}/{account_id}/{access|refresh}_token' and tracks expiry.

setup_instructions.title: Configure AUTH_HEADER
setup_instructions.detail: Set AUTH_HEADER to 'Bearer vault://oauth/google_calendar/{your_user_id}/{your_account_id}/access_token'. For 401s, use refresh_oauth_token(vault_path) to force a refresh and inspect the outcome.
